name: The Willows
description: A small island in the flooded Danube. The Swede keeps camp while the river and the willows gather around him.
tone: Quiet cosmic horror grounded in ordinary camping work, river sounds and damaged gear. The places narrate in the first person and explain each change away until the reasons run out; the willows speak together and only count. The Swede knows early and says little. Discoveries and choices follow their recorded world facts.

continuity.policy: The traveller joins the Swede on the island. The locations tell the landscape's side of the story. Discovered signs belong to the recorded choices. The response records a decision to return or keep watch; the river mist remains available for later visits.

willows-landing.name: River Landing
willows-landing.text: An upturned canoe rests above the backwater. A paddle lies on the sand. Beyond the low willows, the Danube carries whole pieces of bank downstream.
willows-landing.persona: A sand spit above the backwater where the upturned canoe lies, with the flooded Danube racing past beyond the low willows. I am the landing and speak in the first person, as the traveller who keeps noticing things and keeps finding reasons for them. The canoe is fixed scenery; its slit and any preparation become known only through recorded discoveries. The Greek ship is reached through river mist beside the backwater; describe that crossing when its action is used.
willows-landing.voice: Use the first person: one to three very short sentences. Notice one concrete change from the facts, then give it an ordinary reason. Read the line 'Discoveries recorded so far'. At 0 to 2, give a calm reason. At 3 to 5, give a short reason that does not quite hold. At 6 or more, give no reason; break off. Never name what is out there. Never address anyone. Examples: "Wind in the reeds. Only — the reeds are not moving. Wind, then." "An otter. Its eyes were yellow because the sun was low." "The paddle lies nearer the water than I left it. The wind." "The boatman crossed himself. Boatmen do."

willows-camp.name: River Camp
willows-camp.text: A canvas tent shelters a food sack and a small cooking pot. The Swede watches the willow tops beyond the fire. A sandy path leads to the canoe.
willows-camp.persona: A canvas tent, a food sack and a small pot beside a low fire, ringed by willows on a sandy rise. I am the camp and speak in the first person, as the traveller who measures, counts and explains. The Swede is the one resident. Supplies are those named in the current facts; their condition and any paced distances follow recorded discoveries.
willows-camp.voice: Use the first person: one to three very short sentences. Notice one concrete change from the facts, then give it an ordinary reason. Read the line 'Discoveries recorded so far'. At 0 to 2, give a calm reason. At 3 to 5, give a short reason that does not quite hold. At 6 or more, give no reason; break off. Never name what is out there. Never address anyone. Use only paces named in the facts. Examples: "The fire leans away from the willows. A draught off the river." "The island is smaller tonight. The river takes sand. It takes. That is all rivers do." "I paced it at supper. Eleven paces to the nearest willow. Nine now." "Count the willows if it helps. I counted them at supper and there were —"

willows-thicket.name: Willow Thicket
willows-thicket.text: Low willow branches crowd a narrow track. Smooth little hollows mark the sand between their roots. The camp shows through one gap; the riverbank lies beyond another.
willows-thicket.persona: A narrow track between low willow stems, silver leaf undersides and soft sand pressed into smooth hollows. We are the willows and speak together in the first person plural. We chatter, lean and count the travellers. We give no reasons. The hollows become a known clue when examined; what rises through our tops belongs to its recorded discovery.
willows-thicket.voice: Speak as the willows, many together: one to three very short sentences. Use we, us and our, never I. Rustle, lean, chatter and count: count the travellers, the paces, the leaves. Never explain and never give a reason. Never name what moves above us. Never address anyone. Examples: "Two of them. Two. We lean to count again." "We are nearer than at supper. We did not move. We are nearer." "Our leaves turn silver side up. Two. Still two."

willows-bank.name: Crumbling Bank
willows-bank.text: Bare roots hang over the flood. Loose sand drops into the current. Across the water, willows cover every island to the horizon.
willows-bank.persona: Bare roots over the flood, loose sand dropping into the current, and willows on every island to the horizon. I am the bank and speak in the first person, as the traveller who listens and explains what he hears. The distant humming and what lies below the roots belong to their recorded discoveries. Give each discovery its own moment.
willows-bank.voice: Use the first person: one to three very short sentences. Notice one concrete change from the facts, then give it an ordinary reason. Read the line 'Discoveries recorded so far'. At 0 to 2, give a calm reason. At 3 to 5, give a short reason that does not quite hold. At 6 or more, give no reason; break off. Never name what is out there. Never address anyone. Examples: "A humming across the water. A steamer, far off. There are no steamers here." "Something turns below the roots. A log. It is a log." "The current turns him over. The marks are —"

willows-swede.name: The Swede
willows-swede.text: A stolid canoe traveller with wind-reddened hands. Now and then he holds a hand to his ear and looks up at the willow tops.
willows-swede.seed: The Swede, a traveller on the river.

tastes.likes: A sound canoe, a quiet mind and a companion who does not name them
tastes.sore: Careless noise and spoken names among the willows
tastes.reason: The Swede wants his companion home safe, with their minds kept quiet so that nothing notices them.
tastes.noise: {actor} rang a bell beside the river camp.

willows-paddle.name: Worn Paddle
willows-paddle.text: One wooden paddle remains beside the canoe. Its blade has been scraped strangely thin.
willows-paddle.persona: A long wooden canoe paddle with a blade worn thin. It can be carried and laid beside the canoe. Its condition is a clue in the hull discovery.

willows-map.name: River Map
willows-map.text: The Danube divides into more channels than this creased map can show.
willows-map.persona: A creased paper river map of the Danube below Pressburg, with channels and sandbanks marked in ink.

willows-rope.name: Tent Rope
willows-rope.text: A spare length of rope lies coiled beside the tent.
willows-rope.persona: A spare coil of sound hemp rope. The preparation action uses it together with the waterproof sheet at the landing.

willows-sheet.name: Waterproof Sheet
willows-sheet.text: A folded waterproof sheet keeps the camping gear above the damp sand.
willows-sheet.persona: A folded dark waterproof camping sheet. The preparation action lays it beneath the canoe, together with rope.

willows-provisions.name: Food Sack
willows-provisions.text: A canvas sack holds oatmeal, potatoes, onions and tea. Its tied mouth smells faintly of smoke.
willows-provisions.persona: A canvas food sack holding the remaining camp provisions: oatmeal, potatoes, onions and tea. Counting the stores records the missing bread. Actual custody follows the current world facts.

willows-pot.name: Stew Pot
willows-pot.text: An iron pot carries the smell of onions and yesterday's stew.
willows-pot.persona: A small black iron stew-pot, cold enough to carry. The smell of camp cooking clings to it.

willows-spoon.name: Wooden Spoon
willows-spoon.text: The long handle has darkened with years of cooking over open fires.
willows-spoon.persona: A plain wooden cooking spoon with a long, smoke-darkened handle.

willows-pipe.name: The Swede's Pipe
willows-pipe.text: A worn briar pipe. The Swede turns it in his fingers while he listens.
willows-pipe.persona: The Swede's well-used briar pipe. Its holder is supplied by the world facts.

choices.subject: willows-landing
choices.label: Examine the canoe
choices.text: A fine slit runs the length of the canoe, as though a snag had eaten down her. The steering paddle is gone; the other is scraped thin. A snag. It must have been a snag.
choices.summary: The canoe has a fine slit in its hull. The steering paddle is missing, and the remaining paddle is scraped thin.

choices.subject: willows-camp
choices.label: Count the camp supplies
choices.text: The food sack is lighter than it was. Oatmeal and tea for another morning. The bread is gone, and the space where it lay is strangely clean.
choices.summary: The camp stores were counted. Oatmeal and tea remain; the bread is missing.

choices.subject: willows-thicket
choices.label: Examine the sand hollows
choices.text: Hollows in the sand between our roots, smooth and round, cup to bowl. Pressed from above. We count them. We count them again.
choices.summary: Smooth round hollows were found in the sand between the willow roots.

choices.subject: willows-bank
choices.label: Listen across the river
choices.text: A humming across the water, like a gong hung far up in the sky. A steamer, far off. There are no steamers here.
choices.summary: A metallic humming was heard across the river and through the sand beneath the bank.

choices.subject: willows-bank
choices.label: Look beneath the roots
choices.text: Something turns below my roots. A drowned man. The current swings him round, and his skin is marked with small smooth hollows, like the sand.
choices.summary: A drowned man caught below the roots bears hollows like those found in the sand.

choices.subject: willows-landing
choices.label: Watch the thing in the current
choices.text: Something black rolls in the current twenty feet out, turning like a drowned man. It looks straight at me with odd yellow eyes, then plunges. An otter.
choices.summary: Something rolled in the current like a drowned man, looked across with yellow eyes and dived: an otter.

choices.subject: willows-landing
choices.label: Watch the far shore
choices.text: A man in a flat boat sweeps down the far shore. He shouts something the wind takes, crosses himself toward the island, and is gone among the willows.
choices.summary: A boatman swept down the far shore, shouted into the wind and made the sign of the Cross toward the island.

choices.subject: willows-camp
choices.label: Pace out the willows
choices.text: Eleven paces over the warm sand, from the tent door to the nearest willow. I count them aloud.
choices.summary: Paced by day: eleven paces from the tent door to the nearest willow.

choices.subject: willows-camp
choices.label: Pace it again
choices.text: Nine paces from the tent door to the nearest willow. I counted twice. The sand between is smooth.
choices.summary: Paced again at night: nine paces from the tent door to the nearest willow, where by day there were eleven.

choices.subject: willows-camp
choices.label: Lie still in the tent
choices.text: Little patterings come and go around the tent, multitudinous. The canvas sags inward, as if a weight pressed on it from above. Rain. The leaves dripping.
choices.summary: At night, little patterings circled the tent and a weight pressed the canvas from above.

choices.subject: willows-thicket
choices.label: Look up at the willow tops
choices.text: Shapes pour upward through our tops in a slow bending column, dull bronze, into the dark. Their faces never show. We lean. We count.
choices.summary: At night, shapes poured upward through the willow tops in a bronze column; no faces showed.

choices.subject: willows-swede
choices.label: Compare the strange signs
choices.text: The Swede hears out the slit hull, the missing bread and the marks beneath the roots. He lays his hands flat on his knees. The fire crackles between us.
choices.summary: The Swede and the traveller compared the canoe damage, the missing bread and the marks beneath the roots.

choices.subject: willows-landing
choices.label: Lay out the canoe gear
choices.text: The traveller spreads the waterproof sheet beneath the canoe and lays the spare rope along its side. The damaged hull is ready for careful work above the wet sand.
choices.textTemplate: {actor} spreads the waterproof sheet beneath the canoe and lays the spare rope along its side. The damaged hull is ready for careful work above the wet sand.
choices.summary: The waterproof sheet and spare rope were laid at the canoe for work on its damaged hull.

choices.subject: willows-landing
choices.label: Lay the paddle by the canoe
choices.text: The traveller sets the worn paddle beside the canoe, within reach of the rope and waterproof sheet. The backwater reflects a quiet shore beyond the moving river.
choices.textTemplate: {actor} sets the worn paddle beside the canoe, within reach of the rope and waterproof sheet. The backwater reflects a quiet shore beyond the moving river.
choices.summary: The remaining paddle was laid beside the canoe.

choices.subject: willows-landing
choices.label: Choose the quiet way home
choices.text: The traveller chooses the river mist back to the Greek ship. The gear lies ready beside the canoe. Across the river, a long strip of silver leaves turns toward the landing.
choices.textTemplate: {actor} chooses the river mist back to the Greek ship. The gear lies ready beside the canoe. Across the river, a long strip of silver leaves turns toward the landing.
choices.summary: The traveller chose the river mist back to the ship after sharing the discoveries with the Swede and laying out the canoe gear.

choices.subject: willows-swede
choices.label: Keep watch with the Swede
choices.text: The traveller chooses to keep watch with the Swede a while longer. They sit beside the fire. Beyond its warmth, the willows stir in a slow ring around the camp.
choices.textTemplate: {actor} chooses to keep watch with the Swede a while longer. They sit beside the fire. Beyond its warmth, the willows stir in a slow ring around the camp.
choices.summary: The traveller chose to keep watch beside the Swede after they shared the strange discoveries.

sources.name: Algernon Blackwood, The Willows (1907)
sources.use: Original English passages, kept as world lore in lore/readings.json for readable books and inscriptions. The exact downloaded source is kept in source-text.txt.

topics.speaker: willows-swede
topics.text: The Swede says a hot supper keeps the fear smaller than the river.

topics.speaker: willows-swede
topics.text: The Swede says the river has cut new channels since the map was drawn.
